title: Towards Optimal Rack-scale μs-level CPU Scheduling through In-Network Workload Shaping
problem: Prior rack-scale CPU scheduling systems suffer from inaccurate network load balancing and complex sub-optimal scheduling because they lack application awareness. This results in poor tail latency and throughput for microsecond-level services.
motivation: Microsecond-level datacenter services require efficient rack-scale scheduling to achieve near-optimal performance with low tail latency.
method: Pallas performs application-aware in-network workload shaping to partition requests into shards with homogeneous CPU demands. This enables simple yet near-optimal inter-server load balancing, where requests are routed based on CPU affinity. Intra-server scheduling then operates with knowledge of workload characteristics to make near-optimal scheduling decisions.
key_novelty: In-network workload shaping to partition workloads by CPU demand homogeneity, enabling application-aware rack-scale scheduling.
contributions: In-network workload shaping mechanism for preserving CPU demand homogeneity across shards
Application-aware inter-server load balancing and intra-server scheduling approach
Simplified yet near-optimal scheduling algorithms enabled by workload homogeneity
Achieves 8.5x tail latency reduction at medium load and up to 100x at high load compared to RackSched

metrics.speedup: 8.5x tail latency reduction at medium load, up to 100x at high load vs RackSched
